experiment.title: PushBridge
experiment.description: Personal fingertip demonstrations, contact-space policy transfer, target-arm SAC and explicit precision feedback.
experiment.viewer: Recorded MuJoCo state replay with Three.js rendering
experiment.policyInput: Simulator state, not camera images or language
experiment.provenance: Five user-recorded home videos; three training clips, one validation clip and one test clip.
experiment.coordinateUnits: Normalised simulator metres; the real recording's physical scale was not measured.
limitations: State input from simulator, not perception or language
Planar circular-footprint criterion
Follow-up motivated by an observed terminal-metric mismatch
Fresh suite has only one model seed
Twenty paired cases per suite; training seeds are not independent task samples
Known geometry and exact state are supplied to the feedback controller

strategies.label: Direct transfer
strategies.description: The source SAC policy is applied to the compact arm without contact normalisation.

strategies.label: Contact adapter
strategies.description: The source policy is wrapped with a geometric adapter for the compact arm's narrower tool.

strategies.label: Adapter + RL
strategies.description: The adapted source policy receives 20,000 SAC interactions on the compact embodiment.

protocol.question: Does full-object success require a different terminal objective and an explicit precision controller?
protocol.success: Centre distance <= 8 mm throughout ten stationary 0.1 s hold ticks after contact release for hybrid feedback; policy-only starts hold on entering the 8 mm region.

validation.note: One validation run; constants then frozen, no search on evaluation cases.

protocol.policy_weights: Unchanged. No additional imitation updates or RL training.
protocol.attribution: Hybrid policies use learned approach then hand-coded state feedback. Include feedback-only baseline under identical budgets.

export.method: Export deterministic mean actor; two ReLU layers and tanh output; remove training/distribution wrappers

limitations: Local CPU measurements, not edge-hardware measurements
Float32 arithmetic order changes rounding; not bit-identical
Optimization targets the standard SB3 prediction wrapper; the controller and simulator still take time
Thirty timing blocks are repeated measurements on one machine, not independent hardware samples

protocol.question: Is extra SAC training enough, or must the terminal objective match full containment?

strict_objective.objective: 8mm at entry and throughout all10zero-action holdticks

protocol.replay: Each branch starts with empty robot-physics replay; parent checkpoints omitted replay.
protocol.reward: Same compact_potential progress -0.01; +10 stable success; -5 outside. Strict branch changes terminal success predicate only.
protocol.reset_distribution: Unchanged CompactGym: uniform puck/goal ranges, tool40mm behind puck plus2mm noise, friction0.15/0.25/0.40.
protocol.observation: Four contact-normalised relative-state floats from MuJoCo; no vision or language.
protocol.action: Canonical 2D action divided by4/3 contact scale; same joint slew/bounds.

embodiment.name: Compact 3R
embodiment.solver: Damped least squares with joint bounds, command slew limits and a null-space posture preference

validation.use: Diagnostic curves only; final fixed checkpoint, no selection or tuning.

paired.status: Previously inspected cases, retained for paired comparison

fresh.status: Newly declared seed, not previously used for evaluation or tuning

evaluation.hold: Ten zero-action physics ticks; all saved states remain inside. Extra holdticks counted separately.
evaluation.release: Explicit hand-coded release only in finisher and feedback baseline; policy-only uses automatic benchmark hold.

protocol.selection: Train all six final fixed-budget models before evaluating paired or fresh cases; retain every result including regressions.
limitations: Small20case suites; repeated models are not independent task cases
Fresh suite is an in-distribution sample, not new tasks or embodiments
Exact simulator state; no perception, language, hardware or VLA claim
Strict objective was motivated after seeing original failures
Finisher remains engineered state feedback; zero-action hold is benchmark logic
Additional budget alone cannot guarantee improvement; all outcomes reported
